body.x: Solive Ventures Co., Ltd. (CEO Josh Seo) participated in CES 2026 Unveiled, held on January 4 (local time) in Las Vegas, the United States.

Solive Ventures is an edtech startup that has built a differentiated children’s education ecosystem by moving beyond passive, screen-based content and providing experiential learning experiences that stimulate the five senses through direct exploration and hands-on interaction. The company explains that it presents an active participation learning model, in which children and adolescents touch, respond, and think for themselves, as a new industry standard.

In particular, Solive Ventures has verified the educational effectiveness of its content through cooperation with public institutions and international relief and development organizations. By continuously supplying its content to public institutions under the Gangnam District Office and to organizations such as Save the Children, the company has secured extensive references in the B2G market. Based on this track record, it plans to expand significantly into the domestic B2C market starting in 2026.

In addition, Solive Ventures has been increasing its presence in overseas markets by supplying its products through Tinker Labs, which operates an education content supply network across more than 130 countries. Against this backdrop, the company participated in both CES 2026 and the Unveiled event to maximize its global sales impact.

The company’s flagship product, THERATOY, showcased at the event, was introduced as a next-generation, innovative toy designed with proprietary 4D immersive interaction technology. Optimized for children aged three to five, a stage of active brain development, it provides programs that stimulate cognition and thinking skills. By allowing children to touch and manipulate tactile spherical toys, the product supports the natural growth of thinking ability, language skills, and exploratory competence.

The immersive feedback system applied to the product helps reduce side effects associated with visually centered educational content, while enhancing immersion and learning effectiveness through fingertip-based sensory engagement. By promoting learning in a so-called “healthy immersion” state, THERATOY emphasizes the prevention of concerns about excessive media dependence, a common issue among children and adolescents worldwide.

body.cap: Josh Seo, CEO of Solive Ventures, speaks with AVING News reporter Jay Kennedy Markus. | Photo by AVING News

body.x: THERATOY also provides an integrated developmental program that organically connects language learning, particularly English, with cognitive development curricula. Through these broad educational effects, Solive Ventures has accumulated export performance in countries including the United States, Croatia, and Montenegro, and is now pursuing expanded supply in the U.S., the world’s largest edtech market.

A Solive Ventures representative said, “We are pleased to have the opportunity to directly present THERATOY to global media, buyers, and investors through this event,” adding, “Solive Ventures will continue research and development to establish 4D smart participatory education as a new standard in the edtech market and to create an environment where children around the world can learn and grow healthily.”

The representative continued, “To this end, we plan to enter professional edtech content distribution networks in North America and Europe to accelerate market expansion, and to expand networks centered on professional educational institutions such as kindergartens, daycare centers, and preschools. In addition, we will gather feedback from parents around the world through exhibitions and fairs, including CES, and further strengthen our competitiveness in the premium homeschooling market.”

body.cap: Visitors view the Solive Ventures booth at CES 2026 Unveiled. | Photo by AVING News

body.x: Meanwhile, the company will also participate in the leading CES 2026 exhibition, held from January 6 to 9, as part of the Seoul Pavilion located in Eureka Park, the startup-dedicated exhibition zone. The CES 2026 Seoul Pavilion, led by the Seoul Business Agency (SBA), brings together 19 startup support organizations in Seoul, including district offices, related institutions, and universities, to support 70 startups. The participating companies span advanced technology fields such as AI, mobility, and healthcare, and selected outstanding firms receive opportunities to participate in the official CES media event, CES Unveiled.

‘CES Unveiled’ is a key official event held before the CES opening, bringing together Innovation Award winners and companies showcasing cutting-edge products. The event brings together global media, company executives, government officials, and significant technology industry stakeholders in one place.
